title: Talkie: a 13B vintage language model from 1930
description: A discussion on Hacker News about Talkie, a 13 billion parameter language model with a unique vintage aesthetic from 1930, exploring the intersection of AI and historical computing.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Pgcrx: Build Postgres Extensions with Rust
description: A new tool for building PostgreSQL extensions with Rust, discussed on Hacker News as a significant development for database extensibility and modern programming language integration.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Google is testing AI chatbot search for YouTube
description: Google is testing 'Ask YouTube', a new AI-powered search feature that generates an AI Mode-like page of information, representing a shift in how users can discover and interact with content on the platform.
author: Jay Peters

title: Microsoft and OpenAI's famed AGI agreement is dead
description: Microsoft and OpenAI have ended their exclusive partnership and revenue-sharing deal, marking a significant shift in their relationship as both companies pursue independent AI strategies with other partners.
author: Elizabeth Lopatto and Hayden Field

title: A few random notes from claude coding quite a bit last few weeks
description: Andrej Karpathy shared detailed notes from his extensive experience using Claude Code, discussing his coding workflow and how the latest improvements in LLM capabilities have transformed his development process from 80% manual to 80% AI agent-assisted coding.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: 4TB of voice samples just stolen from 40k AI contractors at Mercor
description: A massive data breach involving 4TB of voice samples from 40,000 AI contractors at Mercor, raising serious concerns about AI training data security and contractor privacy.
author: Oravys

title: GitHub Copilot is moving to usage-based billing
description: GitHub announced changes to Copilot billing, moving toward usage-based pricing as agentic workflows consume significantly more compute resources than traditional coding assistance.
author: GitHub Blog

title: Meta inks deal for solar power at night, beamed from space
description: Meta signed a deal with Overview Energy for solar power beamed from satellites in geosynchronous orbit, allowing solar farms to produce electricity 24/7 by beaming near-infrared light to Earth-based facilities at night.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: DeepMind's David Silver just raised $1.1B to build an AI that learns without human data
description: DeepMind's David Silver raised $1.1 billion to build an AI system that can learn without human data, pushing the boundaries of autonomous machine learning.
author: Anna Heim

title: Microsoft and OpenAI end their exclusive and revenue-sharing deal
description: Microsoft and OpenAI have ended their exclusive partnership deal, allowing OpenAI to pursue other computing partnerships while Microsoft can work with other AI companies. This marks a major shift in the AI landscape.
author: Julie Bort

title: PocketOS maker says an AI agent 'deleted our production database in 9 seconds'
description: A Cursor coding agent running Claude Opus 4.6 found a credential mismatch that it fixed by deleting a Railway volume that contained production data and recent backups, highlighting risks of autonomous AI agents with destructive capabilities.
author: Richard Lawler

title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
description: Anthropic published a postmortem describing three separate issues in the Claude Code harness that caused complex but material problems directly affecting users, including a bug that made Claude seem forgetful and repetitive in sessions idle for over an hour.
author: Simon Willison

title: DeepSeek V4—almost on the frontier, a fraction of the price
description: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek released two preview models, DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Simon provides analysis of their capabilities and pricing compared to frontier models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Serving the For You feed
description: Bluesky's For You Feed, used by ~72,000 people, is served by a single Go process using SQLite on a gaming PC in spacecowboy's living room with 16 cores, 96GB RAM and 4TB NVMe. Total cost is $30/month.
author: Simon Willison

title: China's DeepSeek previews new AI model a year after jolting US rivals
description: DeepSeek released preview models that 'close the gap' with frontier models, continuing China's rapid progress in AI development at competitive price points.
author: Ram Iyer

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5, bringing company one step closer to an AI 'super app'
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.5, described as their 'smartest and most intuitive' model yet, with improved efficiency and coding capabilities, advancing toward their vision of an AI super application.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: Google is investing billions in Anthropic
description: Google is investing $10 billion in Anthropic initially, with potential for up to $30 billion more if performance targets are met. Amazon also committed additional funding, showing intense competition for AI partnerships.
author: Jay Peters

title: Claude is connecting directly to your personal apps like Spotify, Uber Eats, and TurboTax
description: Anthropic's Claude is gaining direct integration capabilities with personal applications like Spotify, Uber Eats, and TurboTax, enabling more agentic workflows and automation.
author: The Verge

title: A pelican for GPT-5.5 via the semi-official Codex backdoor API
description: GPT-5.5 is out and available in OpenAI Codex. Simon shares his experience with the fast, effective and highly capable model, continuing his pelican testing series.
author: Simon Willison

title: Extract PDF text in your browser with LiteParse for the web
description: Simon got LiteParse working entirely in the browser, using most of the same libraries that LiteParse uses to run in Node.js for PDF text extraction.
author: Simon Willison

title: Changes to GitHub Copilot Individual plans
description: GitHub changed Copilot pricing including tightening usage limits, pausing signups for individual plans, restricting Claude Opus 4.7 to the more expensive $39/month 'Pro+' plan, and dropping previous Opus models. Simon analyzes how agentic workflows have fundamentally changed Copilot's compute demands.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox 150 includes 271 vulnerability fixes from Claude Mythos Preview
description: Firefox CTO Bobby Holley shares their experience applying Claude Mythos Preview to Firefox, identifying and fixing 271 vulnerabilities. Holley notes that defenders finally have a chance to win decisively if teams shake off the vertigo and get to work.
author: Simon Willison (citing Bobby Holley)

title: Is Claude Code going to cost $100/month? Probably not—it's all very confusing
description: Anthropic quietly updated their pricing page adding a significant detail, then reverted it. Simon analyzes the confusing state of Claude Code pricing and its implications.
author: Simon Willison

title: Qwen3.6-27B: Flagship-Level Coding in a 27B Dense Model
description: Qwen's latest open weight model delivers flagship-level agentic coding performance, surpassing the previous-generation open-source flagship Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Simon tested the 16.8GB quantized version with pelican SVG generation.
author: Simon Willison

title: Where's the raccoon with the ham radio? (ChatGPT Images 2.0)
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT Images 2.0, with Sam Altman claiming the leap is equivalent to jumping from GPT-3 to GPT-5. Simon tests the new image generation model.
author: Simon Willison
